Helix background jobs

Start it, close the tab, come back.

Each button starts a batch of jobs:fetch jobs. The platform makes each request on your behalf after this page's request has ended, so the work keeps going when you close the tab. The page only remembers which jobs it started, in your private data store, so you can come back here or on another device.

Fetch a three-day forecast for eight cities from Open-Meteo, one job per city. The table fills in as the jobs finish.

Eight jobs that each wait ten seconds for an answer. The platform runs at most two jobs at a time for an app, so the batch takes about 40 seconds. Start it, close the tab, and reopen the app after a minute.

Seven jobs, each built to end a particular way: a cancellation, an upstream error, a redirect, a non-JSON answer, an oversized answer, and an origin the app has no grant for. Each row shows what the platform promises next to what actually happened.

Submission probes. These answer immediately and don't use the run history.

The window probe fills the app's per-minute submission allowance on purpose, so jobs you start in the next minute wait before they are submitted.
